confidence_why: Van den Berg's 1995 grammar puts Hunzib stress on the penultimate vowel, but Gamzatov 1975 and Isakov & Khalilov 2012 place it mostly on the initial syllable, Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990 deny word stress altogether, and Borise 2020 concludes there is no agreement.

catalog_quote: 2.5. Hunzib word stress 2.5.1. Position of the stress Hunzib word stress is not fixed, but is generally linked to the prefinal vowel of the word. It is realised as higher intensity, in some cases also as length or tone (2.5.2.). In noun and verb stems word stress usually is on the prefinal vowel, e.g. ... qoqla 'egg', ... hináa 'how?', bədáa 'like this', ... héhe 'hit', -iyáa 'cry'; kišáa 'play ... [p.22:] Long vowels only occur in stressed position, where they are realised with vowel length at least by some (older) informants. Long vowels become plain when word stress shifts to another vowel. E.g.: əg kišaa [kišá(:)] 'he plays' (that/1 play-PRES) əg-ra kiša-baa [k'iša-bá(:)] 'they play' (that-PL play-PL-PRES) ... [§2.5.2:] Hunzib word stress is realised by a higher intensity of the stressed vowel compared with the other vowels of a word. Vowel length can be a concomitant feature of wor…

If Isakov & Khalilov 2012:78-79 and van den Berg's full 2.5 do not support a weight-conditioned right-edge rule, reclassify from 'weight-hedged (final if VV else penult)' to 'contested / weak stress, position disputed (initial vs prefinal vowel)'.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: genuine and correctly located, but confirmed only in held Google Books snippets (feeds_q2/q3/q7/q9/q10/q11/q19/q21), not in a copy consulted of the book; grade 'snippet' is accurate. (2) Deciding source: van den Berg 1995 is a proper reference grammar and the standard English source (also StressTyp2/WALS's source), so the record is not resting on a weak genre. However (a) her own wording is hedged ('not fixed', 'generally', 'usually'), (b) the record's formalisation 'final if long vowel else penult' is StressTyp's syllable translation of her vowel/mora statement and already fails 5/20 of her marked forms per the record's contra, and (c) the open survey downloaded now (Borise 2018 = Oxford Handbook 2020, pp.19-20) places Hunzib explicitly among 'conflicting descriptions': two Russian primary descriptions including the 2012 400-pp grammar say stress is (often) initial, Kib

sources.quote: 'There is no agreement about stress in Hunzib. Bokarev (1967: 474) takes Hunzib stress to be weak and tonal, and "not having a fixed place in the word". According to Gamzatov (1975: 18), Hunzib stress is non-tonal and fixed on the initial syllable. Lomtadze (1984: 145) describes Hunzib as having mobile stress in some paradigms. Kibrik & Kodzasov (1990: 332) propose that Hunzib lacks word stress, but initial syllables carry phrasal accents. Van den Berg (1995: 28) takes Hunzib stress to be penultimate, and notes that it is often accompanied by high pitch, though not for all speakers. Isakov & K
